### Round-1 REDs — closure verified

- **B-1 (KB-RUNTIME / KB-BIJECTION) — closed on both sides.** The source now states the rounding moment in general terms in `rule`, in `baseline.rule` and on all three `delay_allowance_uplift` ladder tiers; the corpus carries it at its own moment in the computation document, beside the other two rounding moments, and once generally in the factor document covering all three tiers. Replayed from the published prose alone on task 0's world, the ceiling now comes to **1,422.57** and the surcharge to **448.17** under half-to-even *and* under half-up — a single value where round 1 yielded a pair (1,422.56/448.16 against 1,422.57/448.17). The masked fall-back remains definite and different (2,713.28 for the ceiling, 800.00 for the surcharge). The sentence is declarative, names no tool, document, problem or customer class, and adds no rounding the source does not state; the replacement worked figures carry fourth decimals and round in both directions (265.4625 → 265.46 down, 105.8875 → 105.89 up) while matching no intermediate or record value of either task.
- **Bench-total domain.** Narrowed on the source side to "every bench labour line standing priced on the work order", which matches its binding; the computation document carries the narrowed wording and a grep over the whole corpus returns **zero** occurrences of the old wording. No scored value moves, since task 0's order carries no priced line that is not a bench labour line.
- **Auditor self-correction.** Revision 1 judged the old bench-total wording "equivalent" — correct as a judgement of the rendering, but I failed to record that the source's prose was wider than its own binding. That belonged in revision 1's policy-side notes and was not there.
- **The three inherited policy-side tensions** (stale rush-surcharge descriptor, per-level goodwill wording, in-workshop state prose) are rendered as the frozen source has them, in documents that are byte-identical to round 1, with nothing added.
